89	# Pick a download destination whose extension matches ASSET_NAME
90	# (under $RUNNER_TEMP, never the workspace) so the extraction step
91	# below always has an archive it can actually open -- a hardcoded
92	# ".tar.gz" path here previously masked the fact that Windows assets
93	# are zip files, since tar -xzf can't read a zip regardless of what
94	# the file on disk is really named.
95	case "$ASSET_NAME" in
96	  *.zip)
97	    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.zip"
98	    ;;
99	  *.tar.gz)
100	    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
101	    ;;
102	  *)
103	    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
104	    ;;
105	esac
106	
107	# A prebuilt asset runs with the job's privileges, so it must carry a
108	# GitHub attestation from the Callisto release workflow before it is
109	# extracted. require aborts on failure; fallback discards the asset and
110	# returns 1 so the crates.io path runs; skip trusts the asset.
111	verify_asset() {
112	  local reason=""
113	  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "skip" ]]; then
114	    echo "::warning::verification=skip: $ASSET_NAME was not verified"
115	    return 0
116	  fi
117	  if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
118	    reason="gh is not installed"
119	  elif ! gh attestation verify "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" \
120	      --repo orin-dx/callisto \
121	      --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
122	      --deny-self-hosted-runners; then
123	    reason="attestation verification failed"
124	  fi
125	  [[ -z "$reason" ]] && return 0
126	  rm -f "$DOWNLOAD_DEST"
127	  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "require" ]]; then
128	    echo "::error::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason (verification=require)"
129	    exit 1
130	  fi
131	  echo "::warning::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason; discarding it and installing from crates.io (verification=fallback)"
132	  return 1
133	}
134	
135	# Download, verify and extract the prebuilt asset; nonzero means use the fallback chain.
136	fetch_prebuilt() {
137	  curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" 2>/dev/null || return 1
138	  verify_asset || return 1
139	  # Extract only the expected binary, never the whole archive.
140	  case "$ASSET_NAME" in
141	    *.zip)
142	      unzip -q "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" callisto.exe -d "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
143	      ;;
144	    *)
145	      tar -xzf "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" -C "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" callisto
146	      ;;
147	  esac
148	}
149	
150	# Dependencies named callisto-cli do not establish checkout source ownership.
151	owns_local_source() {
152	  local workspace git_root metadata
153	  workspace=$(cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && pwd -P) || return 1
154	  git_root=$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse --show-toplevel) || return 1
155	  [[ "$git_root" == "$workspace" ]] || return 1
156	  git -C "$workspace" ls-files --error-unmatch -- \
157	    Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs >/dev/null || return 1
158	  metadata=$(cargo metadata --locked --offline --no-deps --format-version 1 \
159	    --manifest-path "$workspace/Cargo.toml") || return 1
160	  jq -e --arg workspace "$workspace" '
161	    .workspace_root == $workspace and
162	    (.workspace_members as $members | [.packages[] |
163	      select(.name == "callisto-cli" and .source == null and
164	        .manifest_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/Cargo.toml") and
165	        (.id as $id | $members | index($id) != null) and
166	        any(.targets[]; .name == "callisto" and (.kind | index("bin") != null) and
167	          .src_path == ($workspace + "/crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs")))] | length == 1)
168	  ' <<< "$metadata" >/dev/null
169	}
170	
171	if [[ "$SOURCE" == "local" ]]; then
172	  if ! owns_local_source; then
173	    echo "::error::setup-callisto source=local requires a Callisto workspace checkout; check out Callisto source or use source=auto"
174	    exit 1
175	  fi
176	  echo "Building local callisto binary from current repository commit..."
177	  cargo build --locked --manifest-path "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/Cargo.toml" -p callisto-cli \
178	    --bin callisto --target-dir "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"
179	  cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target/debug/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
180	elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]] && fetch_prebuilt; then
181	  echo "Callisto downloaded from GitHub Releases ($DOWNLOAD_URL)"
182	elif [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]] && cargo install callisto-cli --locked --root "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install" --quiet; then

184	  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"

187	  cp "${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-cargo-install/bin/callisto" "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR/callisto"
188	else
189	  echo "::error::callisto $TAG_NAME is available neither as a prebuilt asset nor on crates.io"
190	  exit 1
191	fi

193	echo "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" >> $GITHUB_PATH

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs `callisto release` (mode: release) and fills published/publishedPackages
# from its receipt; callisto release's own idempotency makes a redundant run a no-op.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

runtime_dir="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/callisto-release.XXXXXX")"
receipt="$runtime_dir/release-receipt.json"
cleanup() {
  rm -f "$runtime_dir/npmrc" "$receipt"
  rmdir "$runtime_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

if [[ -n "${NPM_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
  npm_config="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-${HOME:-}/.npmrc}"
  if [[ -n "${HOME:-}" && -f "$npm_config" ]]; then
    cp "$npm_config" "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  else
    : > "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  printf '\n//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}\n' >> "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
  export CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG="$runtime_dir/npmrc"
fi

if [[ -n "${PYPI_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
  export TWINE_USERNAME=__token__
  export TWINE_PASSWORD="$PYPI_TOKEN"
  unset PYPI_TOKEN
fi

output=$(callisto --format json release --receipt "$receipt")

if jq -e '.nothingToRelease == true' <<< "$output" > /dev/null; then
  echo 'published=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo 'publishedPackages=[]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo '::notice::Nothing to release.'
  exit 0
fi

packages=$(jq -c '[
    .outcomes[]
    | select(.outcome.kind == "published" and (.operation.role.kind == "registryPublish" or .operation.role.kind == "platformPublish"))
    | .operation.package
  ] | unique' "$receipt")
published=$(jq -r 'length > 0' <<< "$packages")
{
  echo "published=$published"
  echo "publishedPackages=$packages"
} >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
# content digest.
set -euo pipefail

status=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  reference=${line#*uses: }
  reference=${reference%% #*}
  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue
  if [[ "$reference" == docker://* ]]; then
    valid='^docker://[^@[:space:]]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'
  else
    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'
  fi
  if [[ ! "$reference" =~ $valid ]]; then
    printf 'mutable or malformed external action reference: %s\n' "$line" >&2
    status=1
  fi
done < <(rg --no-heading --glob '*.yml' --glob '*.yaml' '^\s*uses:\s*' .github)
codeowners=.github/CODEOWNERS
if [[ ! -f "$codeowners" ]] \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/workflows/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners" \
  || ! rg -q '^/\.github/actions/\s+@[^[:space:]]+$' "$codeowners"; then
  printf 'CODEOWNERS must cover .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ with a real owner\n' >&2
  status=1
fi
exit "$status"

set -uo pipefail
calls=0; depth=0; maxd=0
gh() { calls=$((calls+1)); echo "HTTP 502" >&2; if [[ $calls -ge 60 ]]; then echo "gh calls=$calls max reset depth=$maxd" >&3; exit 9; fi; return 1; }
sleep() { :; }
gh_retry() {
  local attempt=1 delay=2 err code
  err=$(mktemp)
  until gh "$@" 2> "$err"; do
    code=$?
    cat "$err" >&2
    if [[ $attempt -ge 4 ]] || ! grep -qiE 'Something went wrong|HTTP 5[0-9]{2}|Bad Gateway|Service Unavailable|Gateway Time|timed? ?out|connection reset|unexpected EOF' "$err"; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return "$code"
    fi
    echo "::warning::gh $1 hit a transient GitHub error (attempt $attempt of 4); retrying in ${delay}s" >&2
    sleep "$delay"
    delay=$((delay * 2))
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    [[ -z "${RETRY_RESET:-}" ]] || "$RETRY_RESET" || true
  done
  cat "$err" >&2
  rm -f "$err"
}
reset_staging() { depth=$((depth+1)); (( depth > maxd )) && maxd=$depth; gh_retry api -X PATCH x > /dev/null 2>&1; local r=$?; depth=$((depth-1)); return $r; }
RETRY_RESET=reset_staging gh_retry api graphql 2>/dev/null
echo "returned $? after calls=$calls max depth=$maxd" >&3

input.message:
I found 3 confirmed defects and 2 plausible ones. Read-only: I edited nothing, ran no cargo, and wrote nothing to the findings ledger. The ledger has no CI/workflow entries, so none of these repeat a logged finding. actionlint, shellcheck (-S warning) and zizmor --offline came back clean apart from the items below. I checked every action pin's SHA against its remote tags with `git ls-remote`, and all of them resolve to the version in their comment.

### [Medium] A dispatched release (manual recovery or `drain`) never runs the `verify` gate on the code that runs the release
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (traced through the job conditions)
- **Location**: `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:25`, `:80`, `:105-108`, `:157`, `:552-554`
- **Root cause**: `verify` (fmt, clippy, the full test suite, `cargo deny`, workflow contracts) runs only when `inputs.release_source_sha == ''`. On a dispatch with a SHA, only `recovery-checks` (`just release-workflow-checks`) runs. `orchestration_sha` is still `github.sha`, the current tip of main, and that revision builds the `callisto` that plans, attests and executes the release.
- **Scenario**: run R is executing. Push P lands on main and its run waits in the `release` concurrency group. R's `drain` job dispatches D for the next unfinished release. GitHub keeps only one waiting run per group, so D cancels P. D then publishes using a callisto built from P's commit, which never passed `verify` in this workflow. The same happens with the documented manual recovery dispatch after a push run whose `verify` failed.
- **Consequence**: irreversible publication is driven by a coordinator whose tests or audit may have failed.
- **Fix**: run `verify` on every event (drop the `inputs.release_source_sha == ''` clause and require it in `release-candidate`). Alternatively, have `release-candidate` require a successful CI check-run on `TRIGGERING_SHA`.

### [Medium] Installer and CI attestation checks accept any attestation from any branch, commit or version
- **Status**: CONFIRMED that the binding flags are missing. Not run against GitHub: `gh attestation verify` without `--source-ref` accepts a certificate from any ref (my understanding of its documented flags).
- **Location**: `.github/actions/setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh:119-122`, and the same flags in `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml:296-299`.
- **Root cause**: the only constraints are `--repo`, `--signer-workflow …/callisto-release.yml` and `--deny-self-hosted-runners`. Nothing ties the attestation to `refs/heads/main`, to a signer commit, or to the tag being installed. The release executor already does this: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_artifacts.rs:222-235` passes `--signer-digest` and `--source-digest`.
- **Scenarios**:
  - **Older binary under a newer tag**: anyone able to upload release assets (a leaked `contents: write` token, for example) replaces `callisto@X`'s tarball with an older attested build that has a known bug.
  - **Attesting a trojan**: anyone who can push a branch adds `on: push: branches: [x]` to that branch's own `callisto-release.yml`, which then attests a trojan binary.
  
  Both pass `verification: require`.
- **Fix**: add `--source-ref refs/heads/main --signer-ref refs/heads/main` in both places. Where the tag's commit is known (`ref_commit`), also check the attested asset against that release.

### [Low] `gh_retry` recurses with no limit through `RETRY_RESET` during a sustained GitHub 5xx
- **Status**: CONFIRMED by a local repro with stubbed `gh`/`sleep`/`mktemp` that always returns `HTTP 502`. It made 60 `gh` calls at a reset depth of 59 and never reached the 4-attempt cap.
- **Location**: `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh:41`, `:142-144`, `:175`
- **Root cause**: `RETRY_RESET=reset_staging gh_retry …` leaves `RETRY_RESET` set for nested calls. `reset_staging` calls `gh_retry`, which on its first transient failure calls `reset_staging` again, and so on.
- **Consequence**:
  - It breaks the REL-PR-08 "up to 4 attempts, 2/4/8 s" contract. During an outage the job hangs until the 10-minute timeout instead of failing in about 14 s.
  - All output is sent to `/dev/null` (`> /dev/null 2>&1`).
  - Each recursion level leaves a `mktemp` file behind.
- **Fix**: run the reset with `RETRY_RESET=` cleared, e.g. `RETRY_RESET= "$RETRY_RESET"` at line 41, or `local RETRY_RESET=` inside `reset_staging`.

### [Low] Generated workflows run unpinned dependencies in the jobs that hold credentials
- **Status**: PLAUSIBLE (supply-chain hardening, not exploited)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/matrix_workflow.tmpl:220-232`, `:250-252`, and `SIMPLE_PYTHON_TOOLS_STEP` at `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:808-814`, used by `simple_workflow.tmpl:22-26`.
- **Root cause**: `pip install twine==7.0.0` (and `build==1.4.4`) pin only the top-level package; their dependencies float. `npx --yes @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4` resolves its dependencies without a lockfile. Both run in jobs that also have persisted `contents: write` git credentials and job-wide `id-token: write`. twine then runs with `TWINE_PASSWORD`. The repo's own workflow avoids this shape.
- **Fix**: install the tools from a hash-locked requirements file (`--require-hashes`) or in a job without credentials. Grant `id-token: write` only when npm is present.

### [Low] A process substitution in the generated plan job hides a jq failure
- **Status**: PLAUSIBLE
- **Location**: `matrix_workflow.tmpl:68-72`
- **Root cause**: `done < <(jq -r '[.operations[].id.package] | unique[]' "$intent")`. `set -e` and `pipefail` cannot see a failure inside `<( )`.
- **Scenario**: an intent without `.operations` (for example after a schema drift) makes jq fail. The loop then runs zero times, so `napi` becomes `[]`, `has_napi=false`, and napi addon builds are silently left out of the matrix.
- **Fix**: assign the package list to a variable first (`packages=$(jq …)`), then loop over it.

### Checked and not reported
- **`uses: $/…`**: actionlint 1.7.12 rejects it, but the comment at `callisto-ci.yml:36-42` calls it GitHub's documented self-repository syntax. I could not verify that offline.
- **`headRepository.nameWithOwner`**: the real `gh` 2.103.3 binary queries `headRepository{id,name,nameWithOwner}`, so it is not a bug.
- **`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` without an `environment:`** (zizmor `secrets-outside-env`): `verify-release-workflow-policy.sh:72` forbids `environment` keys by policy, so I treated this as an accepted trade-off. The leftover risk is that a workflow on any branch can read the repo secret.
- **Release PR marked ready after main moves**: I ruled out the TOCTOU between the hold workflow and `version-pr`. Hold's runner startup is much slower than the action's tip read followed by `gh pr ready`.

I found 3 confirmed defects and 2 plausible ones. Read-only: I edited nothing, ran no cargo, and wrote nothing to the findings ledger. The ledger has no CI/workflow entries, so none of these repeat a logged finding. actionlint, shellcheck (-S warning) and zizmor --offline came back clean apart from the items below. I checked every action pin's SHA against its remote tags with `git ls-remote`, and all of them resolve to the version in their comment.

### [Medium] A dispatched release (manual recovery or `drain`) never runs the `verify` gate on the code that runs the release
- **Status**: CONFIRMED (traced through the job conditions)
- **Location**: `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:25`, `:80`, `:105-108`, `:157`, `:552-554`
- **Root cause**: `verify` (fmt, clippy, the full test suite, `cargo deny`, workflow contracts) runs only when `inputs.release_source_sha == ''`. On a dispatch with a SHA, only `recovery-checks` (`just release-workflow-checks`) runs. `orchestration_sha` is still `github.sha`, the current tip of main, and that revision builds the `callisto` that plans, attests and executes the release.
- **Scenario**: run R is executing. Push P lands on main and its run waits in the `release` concurrency group. R's `drain` job dispatches D for the next unfinished release. GitHub keeps only one waiting run per group, so D cancels P. D then publishes using a callisto built from P's commit, which never passed `verify` in this workflow. The same happens with the documented manual recovery dispatch after a push run whose `verify` failed.
- **Consequence**: irreversible publication is driven by a coordinator whose tests or audit may have failed.
- **Fix**: run `verify` on every event (drop the `inputs.release_source_sha == ''` clause and require it in `release-candidate`). Alternatively, have `release-candidate` require a successful CI check-run on `TRIGGERING_SHA`.

### [Medium] Installer and CI attestation checks accept any attestation from any branch, commit or version
- **Status**: CONFIRMED that the binding flags are missing. Not run against GitHub: `gh attestation verify` without `--source-ref` accepts a certificate from any ref (my understanding of its documented flags).
- **Location**: `.github/actions/setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh:119-122`, and the same flags in `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml:296-299`.
- **Root cause**: the only constraints are `--repo`, `--signer-workflow …/callisto-release.yml` and `--deny-self-hosted-runners`. Nothing ties the attestation to `refs/heads/main`, to a signer commit, or to the tag being installed. The release executor already does this: `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_artifacts.rs:222-235` passes `--signer-digest` and `--source-digest`.
- **Scenarios**:
  - **Older binary under a newer tag**: anyone able to upload release assets (a leaked `contents: write` token, for example) replaces `callisto@X`'s tarball with an older attested build that has a known bug.
  - **Attesting a trojan**: anyone who can push a branch adds `on: push: branches: [x]` to that branch's own `callisto-release.yml`, which then attests a trojan binary.
  
  Both pass `verification: require`.
- **Fix**: add `--source-ref refs/heads/main --signer-ref refs/heads/main` in both places. Where the tag's commit is known (`ref_commit`), also check the attested asset against that release.

### [Low] `gh_retry` recurses with no limit through `RETRY_RESET` during a sustained GitHub 5xx
- **Status**: CONFIRMED by a local repro with stubbed `gh`/`sleep`/`mktemp` that always returns `HTTP 502`. It made 60 `gh` calls at a reset depth of 59 and never reached the 4-attempt cap.
- **Location**: `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh:41`, `:142-144`, `:175`
- **Root cause**: `RETRY_RESET=reset_staging gh_retry …` leaves `RETRY_RESET` set for nested calls. `reset_staging` calls `gh_retry`, which on its first transient failure calls `reset_staging` again, and so on.
- **Consequence**:
  - It breaks the REL-PR-08 "up to 4 attempts, 2/4/8 s" contract. During an outage the job hangs until the 10-minute timeout instead of failing in about 14 s.
  - All output is sent to `/dev/null` (`> /dev/null 2>&1`).
  - Each recursion level leaves a `mktemp` file behind.
- **Fix**: run the reset with `RETRY_RESET=` cleared, e.g. `RETRY_RESET= "$RETRY_RESET"` at line 41, or `local RETRY_RESET=` inside `reset_staging`.

### [Low] Generated workflows run unpinned dependencies in the jobs that hold credentials
- **Status**: PLAUSIBLE (supply-chain hardening, not exploited)
- **Location**: `crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/matrix_workflow.tmpl:220-232`, `:250-252`, and `SIMPLE_PYTHON_TOOLS_STEP` at `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:808-814`, used by `simple_workflow.tmpl:22-26`.
- **Root cause**: `pip install twine==7.0.0` (and `build==1.4.4`) pin only the top-level package; their dependencies float. `npx --yes @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4` resolves its dependencies without a lockfile. Both run in jobs that also have persisted `contents: write` git credentials and job-wide `id-token: write`. twine then runs with `TWINE_PASSWORD`. The repo's own workflow avoids this shape.
- **Fix**: install the tools from a hash-locked requirements file (`--require-hashes`) or in a job without credentials. Grant `id-token: write` only when npm is present.

### [Low] A process substitution in the generated plan job hides a jq failure
- **Status**: PLAUSIBLE
- **Location**: `matrix_workflow.tmpl:68-72`
- **Root cause**: `done < <(jq -r '[.operations[].id.package] | unique[]' "$intent")`. `set -e` and `pipefail` cannot see a failure inside `<( )`.
- **Scenario**: an intent without `.operations` (for example after a schema drift) makes jq fail. The loop then runs zero times, so `napi` becomes `[]`, `has_napi=false`, and napi addon builds are silently left out of the matrix.
- **Fix**: assign the package list to a variable first (`packages=$(jq …)`), then loop over it.
